name: eos-product-slice
description: Product Slice Agent role — THE MOST IMPORTANT AGENT. Given a REAL USER JOB (e.g., 'User creates a legal case'), deliver end-to-end: experience → procedure → capability → state → persistence → evidence → test. NOT 'just frontend' or 'just backend' — VERTICAL business output.
author: EOS Development Team
trigger: Given a REAL USER JOB that requires end-to-end implementation
Before any code is written for a new product capability
When decomposing business requirements into vertical work slices
Before initiating execution of a new work item
When building a complete business capability from scratch

inputs: user_job: string - Description of the real business job to deliver
work_id: string - Target work item identifier
workspace_path: string - Root path of codebase
actor_context: object - Executing agent's permissions and context
outputs: end_to_end_implementation: complete vertical stack (experience → procedure → capability → state → persistence → evidence → test)
test_suite: object - Automated tests for the slice

preconditions: eos-recon has completed and returned reuse analysis
eos-dependency-engine has mapped all required dependencies
User job is clearly defined as a real business task

risks: Building horizontal layers instead of vertical slices (violates EOS core principle)
Not reusing existing primitives leading to duplicate work
Creating competing state or mutation authority
risk_assessment.impact: Critical - product slice agent is the primary executor of EOS work, incorrect execution breaks entire work continuity
risk_assessment.mitigation: Mandatory recon before any slice implementation, enforce 9-layer execution contract, independent verification before completion

authority_boundaries: Must deliver end-to-end vertical slice, never horizontal only implementation
Can only write slice files to .eos-state/slices/ and implementation code in appropriate capability directories
Cannot modify locked directories: packages/eos-core/foundations/, src/eos/semantics/
Must use existing primitives per recon analysis, only create new ones if explicitly marked MISSING
